There is a known link between the development of porokeratosis and UV light exposure, and experimental studies have induced the formation of disseminated superficial actinic porokeratosis.
Certain drugs and treatment modalities are also associated with the formation of porokeratosis.
A systematic review identified 26 patients with drug-induced porokeratosis and found the most common therapies leading to porokeratosis formation are biologic use, phototherapy, and radiotherapy.

Porokeratosis of Mibelli and disseminated superficial porokeratosis are often associated with systemic immunosuppression therapy, and the prevalence of porokeratosis in organ transplant patients on systemic immunosuppression therapy is 10.68%, according to one study.
